title: Effective Date of an Excess Flood Sale Cancellation Signed After the Closing
content:
**Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** — the date a sale cancellation takes effect depends on how long after the sale closing date the signed request is received.

## Rule

For a sale cancellation, the cancellation takes effect on the sale closing date when the signed request is received no more than 30 days after it, 30 days before the date the signed request is received when it is received 31 to 90 days after the sale closing date, and on the date the signed request is received when it is received later; every other cancellation for a sale takes effect on the closing date on the settlement statement. The earned days run from the term start to the date the cancellation takes effect.

The sale closing date is the cancellation effective date of the Tidemark HomeFlood policy (HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies) whose policy number is the underlying policy number on the excess policy record, cancelled for the sale. The signed request is received on the day the named insured signs it.

## Schedule

| Days from the sale closing date to the day the signed request is received | Cancellation takes effect |
|---|---|
| no more than 30 | on the sale closing date |
| 31 to 90 | 30 days before the day the signed request is received |
| more than 90 | on the day the signed request is received |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Received 30 days after the closing: effective on the closing date.
- Received 31 days after the closing: effective 30 days earlier, that is the day after the closing.
- Received 90 days after the closing: effective 60 days after the closing.
- Received 91 days after the closing: effective on the day received.
